LanguageData.SEC_Hediff_Tail_Ritual_Cutoff.label: Ritual Cutoff
LanguageData.SEC_Hediff_Tail_Ritual_Cutoff.descriptio: The tail is ritual cutoff. In ancient Alfau peninsula culture, ritual tail cutoff was a way to mark lowly or despicable Alfaus like public-owned slaves, exiles, criminals and whores. Different from branding, ritual tail cutoff won't leave long-term scars, the tail can still grow back to its natural length after some time, this also means that regular trimming is required, to maintain ritual shape. The ritual process itself was also one of the ways ancient communes emphasized their authority.\n\nAfter the founding of the People's State of Alfau, ritual tail cutoff has been declared abolished and prohibited by law, but in remote rural areas some communes still retain it as illegal punishment or religious rituals, the Alfaus living in foreign countries also did not abandon this traditional ritual. Even on the other side of the Cold War Iron Curtain, in the underground society of the Union of Liberalist Republics, some gangs composed of Alfaus make ritual tail cutoff their initiation ceremony.
